titel: Shelf life: salt and sugar bind water
kurz: Germs need free water. Salt, sugar and drying bind it up, which is why honey, jam, salami and dried fruit spoil so slowly.
bild_im_kopf: Like an oasis where every drop is already taken: newcomers find nothing left to drink.
was_passiert: What counts is not just the water content, but how much water is freely available (water activity). Salt and sugar bind water to themselves; drying removes it. Most dangerous bacteria need a lot of free water; mould and some yeasts manage with less. That is why jam can go mouldy, but honey hardly ever does.
warum_wichtig: Explains why jam needs enough sugar, why salami keeps without a fridge and why reduced-sugar jam belongs in the fridge.
synonyme: why honey does not go mouldy
faustregeln: Keep reduced-sugar jam in the fridge once opened.
Store dried fruit and nuts dry and sealed.
Salt, sugar and drying do not replace hygiene; they only slow germs down.

praxis.text: Jam with lots of sugar keeps for a long time unopened, honey almost indefinitely.
Cured ham and salami keep thanks to salt and drying.
